
### Preprocessing Training Data

```{r}
# Preprocessing function
# Load necessary libraries
library(tm)
library(SnowballC)
library(readxl)
library(e1071)
library(caret)

# Define the preprocessing function
preprocess_tweet <- function(tweet) {
  # Check if the tweet is non-empty
  if (is.na(tweet) || tweet == "") {
    return("")
  }
  
  # Lowercase
  tweet <- tolower(tweet)
  
  # Replace different spellings of 'zelenskyy' with 'zelenskyy'
  tweet <- gsub("zelensk[iy]+", "zelenskyy", tweet)
  
  # Remove URLs
  tweet <- gsub("http\\S+|www\\S+", "", tweet)
  
  # Remove hashtags
  tweet <- gsub("#\\S+", "", tweet)
  
  # Remove punctuation and numbers
  tweet <- removePunctuation(tweet)
  tweet <- removeNumbers(tweet)
  
  # Remove extra white spaces
  tweet <- stripWhitespace(tweet)
  
  
  # Remove stopwords
  tweet <- removeWords(tweet, stopwords("en"))
  
  # Stemming
  tweet <- wordStem(words = tweet, language = "en")
  
  return(paste(tweet, collapse = " "))
}

# Load the training data from the Excel file
training_data <- read_excel("/Users/sudharsanajagatheesh/Desktop/Training.xlsx")

# Check if 'Tweet' column exists
if (!"tweet" %in% colnames(training_data)) {
  stop("The 'Tweet' column does not exist in the data frame.")
}

# Apply the preprocessing function to the 'Tweet' column
training_data$Processed_Tweet <- sapply(training_data$tweet, preprocess_tweet, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

# Verify the results
head(training_data$Processed_Tweet)


```

##Naive Bayes training
```{r}
# Convert 'Sentiment' column to a factor
training_data$Sentiment <- as.factor(training_data$sentiment)

library(caret)

# Partition the data into training and testing sets
set.seed(123) # for reproducibility
index <- createDataPartition(training_data$sentiment, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- training_data[index, ]
test_data <- training_data[-index, ]


```

### Creating DTMS

```{r}
library(e1071)

# Train the Naive Bayes model
nb_model <- naiveBayes(train_matrix, train_data$sentiment)

```

```{r}
# Assuming the 'Text' column contains the preprocessed tweets
train_corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(train_data$Processed_Tweet))
test_corpus <- Corpus(VectorSource(test_data$Processed_Tweet))

# Create DTMs
train_dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(train_corpus)
test_dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(test_corpus, control = list(dictionary = Terms(train_dtm)))

# Convert DTMs to matrices
train_matrix <- as.matrix(train_dtm)
test_matrix <- as.matrix(test_dtm)

# Ensure that the number of columns in both matrices are the same
if (ncol(train_matrix) != ncol(test_matrix)) {
  stop("The number of features in the training and testing sets are different.")
}

```

### Inspecting Data
```{r}
# Check the structure and summary of predictions and actual labels
str(predictions)
str(test_data$Sentiment)
table(predictions)
table(test_data$Sentiment)

```
```{r}
# Assuming 'nb_model' is your trained Naive Bayes model and 'test_matrix' is prepared for test data
predictions <- predict(nb_model, test_matrix)

```

## Making Predictions
```{r}

# When subsetting or preparing test_data, ensure factor levels are retained
test_data$Sentiment <- factor(test_data$sentiment, levels = c("1", "-1", "0"))

# Relevel both actual and predicted sentiments to include all possible levels
test_data$sentiment <- factor(test_data$sentiment, levels = all_levels)
predictions <- factor(predictions, levels = all_levels)

# Now attempt to create the confusion matrix again
performance <- confusionMatrix(predictions, test_data$sentiment)
print(performance)


```

```{r}
library(reticulate)

# Ensure tweets are in a Python list and sentiments are in a numpy array
tweets_list <- training_data$tweet
sentiments_array <- as.integer(training_data$sentiment) + 1  # Adjusting sentiment values to start from 0

# Insert actual data into Python code

python_code <- gsub("sentiments = \\[\\]", sprintf("sentiments = %s", py_str(sentiments_array)), python_code)

# Execute Python code
py_run_string(python_code)
```
